recent.subject: Release notes: fill in what Luna's accuracy check found missing
Fix versus seating and results, grid Continue in co-op (v0.33.1)

entries.title: Versus and menu fixes
entries.html:
• In online versus, a joining player now sees the host on the scoreboard and in the opponents panel.
  • A guest who wins is told they won, not "Player 3 wins".
  • You can host your most recent canvas online straight from its Continue card.
  • The join panel says you joined once the board has arrived.

entries.title: Safer online play
entries.html:
• In a game with two or more guests, one guest could pretend to be the host: push a board at the others, fake or cancel a match, or disconnect another guest, which could end a match for everyone. That's no longer possible.
  • Joining a friend's game no longer makes your own solo progress on that canvas look empty.
  • Nobody can fill a room with fake players to keep your friends out.
  • During a versus match, nobody can stitch on your board or replace it, and sudoku digits only count between "Go!" and the final whistle.
  • The online library now ships with the game instead of loading from another site, and online play works when you open the game file straight off disk.
  • The versus lobby says plainly that each player reports their own score.

entries.title: Versus mode
entries.html:
• Race up to three friends for the canvas, on one screen or online with a code.
  • On one screen you share the canvas, and each region goes to whoever stitched most of it. A nearly finished region can still be stolen.
  • Online, everyone solves their own copy of the same puzzle. You see your rivals' progress and a minimap of where they're working, never their colours.
  • Three rules: play out the full canvas, first to a number of regions, or most regions when the clock stops.
  • A match never touches your saved progress.
  • During a match, region quotes appear as a small notice instead of a dialog over the board.
  • Fixed: sudoku digits placed with a mouse or controller now count for the player who placed them, touch stitches in split-screen go to the right player, and players 2 to 4 can undo their own moves.

entries.title: A brand-new puzzle from any canvas
entries.html:
• "New weave" in the menu gives any canvas a completely different puzzle: same painting and regions, new solution and clues.
  • Each weave keeps its own save, so you can go back to the original and pick up where you left off.
  • Share codes and co-op carry the weave, so friends get the same puzzle.

entries.title: No more waiting to start
entries.html:
• Every canvas ships ready-made. Opening one used to take up to 35 seconds the first time. Now it's the length of the loading animation.
  • Every player gets exactly the same puzzle on every browser.

entries.title: See your progress on the canvas cards
entries.html:
• Map cards show the regions you've finished in full colour, plus a progress bar. They never show anything you haven't earned.
  • Resetting a canvas clears its card too.

entries.title: A calmer interface
entries.html:
• The top bar is one tidy row, with extra actions in a ⋯ menu.
  • Options has sections for colour, music, difficulty and controller.
  • The loading screen, home menu and canvas grid are clearer, and Continue shows your progress and play time.

entries.title: New canvas, In-and-Out
entries.html: • A new 237×158 canvas with 25 regions, 8 sudoku plots and 8 picross patches.

entries.title: Clearer controller setup
entries.html: • The Xbox and PlayStation column headings in controller setup are easier to read.

entries.title: Bigger controller buttons
entries.html: • Controller button icons are larger and line up under their headings.

entries.title: Controller icon polish
entries.html: • PlayStation's triangle matches the other symbols, and button labels are lighter.

entries.title: Controller buttons in their real colours
entries.html: • Controller setup draws each button the way it looks on the real pad.

entries.title: PlayStation buttons in controller setup
entries.html: • Controller setup lists PlayStation buttons next to Xbox ones.

entries.title: Coming back to a canvas is near-instant
entries.html:
• A canvas you've already played opens in about a second. Angels went from about 37 seconds to under one. A difficulty you haven't tried yet still has to be woven the first time.
  • Picross patches get harder with the difficulty, and every one is still solvable by logic alone.
  • Changing difficulty never redraws a patch you've already started.

entries.title: Personal co-op moments
entries.html:
• In co-op, the "four mistakes" prompt goes only to the player who made them, and "Clear my errors" clears only your tiles.
  • Region quotes go to the players who helped finish that region. Everyone else gets a notice and can read it if they like.
  • Controllers can press the buttons on quotes and prompts.

entries.title: Clearer Save button
entries.html: • Saving your progress has its own 💾 button. The dialog explains how to hand your board to a friend, and warns that importing one replaces their progress on that canvas.

entries.title: New canvas, Inferno
entries.html: • A 184×164 canvas with 52 hand-drawn regions.

entries.title: Play on phones and tablets
entries.html:
• Tap or drag to stitch, two fingers to pan and zoom, and a light or dark brush switch. Tap a sudoku cell to select it, and tap again to change its digit.
  • Typing a code or PIN no longer triggers board shortcuts.
  • Your last stitch is saved even if you close the tab right away.
  • The music setting is remembered, and with music off the track isn't downloaded at all.
  • Co-op undo takes back only your own moves.
  • Friends on slightly different versions can still play together.

entries.title: Music from the start
entries.html: • Music starts at the home menu.

entries.title: A visual tutorial
entries.html: • "How to play" shows the rules with small tile diagrams.

entries.title: Cozy menu
entries.html: • The home menu is centred, with a soft moving background that never shows any artwork.

entries.title: Menu fixes
entries.html: • Clicking outside any dialog closes it, and controller setup opens above Options.

entries.title: The timer remembers your time
entries.html: • Each canvas keeps its own play time and counts only while you're playing.

entries.title: A classic home menu
entries.html:
• Single Player, Co-op, Continue, Options and Credits in one list.
  • Continue jumps back into your last canvas.
  • Sort the canvas grid by name, date added or size.

entries.title: Options menu
entries.html:
• Recolour the whole interface with presets or a hue slider.
  • Music volume and a default difficulty for new canvases.

entries.title: Home menu and canvas picker
entries.html:
• The game opens on a menu: pick Single Player or Co-op, then a canvas.
  • Host or join online co-op from the menu.

entries.title: New name
entries.html: • The game is now "One More Tile: The Emergent Canvas". Your progress carries over.

entries.title: Clear errors any time
entries.html: • A toolbar button sweeps away every wrong tile whenever you like.

entries.title: Dragging paints every square
entries.html: • A drag paints every square it crosses, so fixing a run of mistakes takes one stroke.

entries.title: Pan while loading
entries.html: • Move around the board with the middle mouse button while it loads.

entries.title: New canvas, Angels
entries.html: • A 204×136 canvas with 20 regions.

entries.title: No more skip prompt
entries.html: • The "click to skip" prompt is gone, since skipping couldn't speed anything up.

entries.title: Loading progress and zoom
entries.html:
• A readable title card and a real progress bar while the board loads.
  • Zoom in during loading to watch the clues appear.

entries.title: Loading paced to the canvas
entries.html: • Bigger canvases get a slower, steadier loading animation.

entries.title: Watch the canvas being woven
entries.html: • The loading screen shows the puzzle being made, without spoiling it.

entries.title: No pre-filled squares, ever
entries.html:
• Every tile is yours to stitch. The game used to fill in a few where logic stalled.
  • After updating, a few old marks may show as mistakes. "Clear my errors" fixes them.

entries.title: New canvas, Amigos
entries.html: • A 144×95 canvas with 10 regions.

entries.title: Clean finished art
entries.html: • Finished regions no longer show faint lines between tiles.

entries.title: Esc closes dialogs
entries.html: • Esc closes whatever dialog is open.

entries.title: Keep a co-op board
entries.html: • Guests can save the shared board as their own progress.

entries.title: Dialog fix
entries.html: • Dialog buttons wrap on narrow screens.

entries.title: Up to four players
entries.html:
• Local and online co-op for two to four players, and friends can join any time.
  • Split-screen fits any window size.

entries.title: Controller follows the mouse
entries.html: • The controller cursor starts where you last clicked.

entries.title: Online co-op
entries.html: • Host a game, share a short code, and solve the same board live with a friend, cursors and all.

entries.title: Split-screen co-op
entries.html: • Two players on one screen, each with their own cursor and view.

entries.title: Testing tool
entries.html: • A developer option in the PIN-locked solver.

entries.title: Regions wait for their puzzles
entries.html: • A region reveals only once the sudoku and picross inside it are solved too.

entries.title: Every tile counts
entries.html: • A region reveals only when every tile is marked, dark ones included.

entries.title: Reliability fixes
entries.html:
• Clearing your last mistakes can finish a region.
  • No region strands a few tiles inside another one. On Flash, two stray tiles went back to the region around them.

entries.title: Big canvases load smoothly
entries.html: • Large canvases no longer freeze the page while they load.

entries.title: New canvas, Blinding Lights
entries.html: • A new, more detailed canvas.

entries.title: New canvas, Flash
entries.html: • Its name reveals itself region by region as you solve.

entries.title: Music
entries.html:
• Background music in the header.
  • The 3×3 highlight stays inside the current region.
  • The header works on small screens.

entries.title: Undo fix
entries.html: • Undo takes back one controller tile at a time.

entries.title: Quotes for The Fighters
entries.html: • Six regions of The Fighters canvas have a character quote.

entries.title: New canvas, The Fighters
entries.html: • A third canvas, with its own saved progress.

entries.title: Region quotes
entries.html:
• Finishing some regions shows a character quote, and you can replay it by clicking the region.
  • Solved picross patches stay in colour after a reload.

entries.title: More canvases
entries.html:
• Several canvases, each with its own saved progress and its own puzzle.
  • Regions follow the edges in the painting, so each finished region shows a recognisable piece of it.
  • Share your progress as a code or a file.
  • A play timer.

entries.title: Hints and undo
entries.html:
• Undo, a 3×3 highlight under the cursor, and hints that explain the move.
  • The easier tiers need only plain counting.

entries.title: First release
entries.html: • A fill-a-pix puzzle with sudoku and picross mixed in, five difficulty tiers, gamepad support and autosave. Solving it reveals a pixel-art painting.
